title: Chinese vessels in West PH Sea increased to 48 after ASEAN Summit 2026 --AFP
summary: The number of Chinese vessels monitored in the West Philippine Sea increased to 48 in the past week following the ASEAN Summit 2026, the Armed Forces of the Philippines said on Tuesday.

blocks.text: The number of Chinese vessels monitored in the West Philippine Sea (WPS) increased to 48 in the past week following the ASEAN Summit 2026, the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) said on Tuesday.

Interviewed on Super Radyo dzBB, AFP spokesperson for the WPS (ret.) Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad said 48 Chinese vessels were recorded from November 17 to 23. This was higher compared to the 19 Chinese vessels recorded from November 9 to 16.
“Noong ASEAN (Summit), nagpakita sila na kaunti na ang nilagay nila sa ating EEZ na mga barko,” Trinidad said.
(During ASEAN [Summit], they showed that they have deployed just a few ships in our EEZ.)
Trinidad said the Philippines continues its efforts to monitor foreign vessels in its maritime domain through its sea-based, air-based, land-based, and space-based monitoring capabilities.
He also cited the contributions of civilian maritime auxiliaries, particularly Filipino fisherfolk and seafarers, who provide photographs, videos, and reports of foreign vessel movements.
Trinidad said the information provided by civilians supplements the military's monitoring capabilities, allowing the Philippines to know almost in real time when foreign vessels enter its waters.

Tensions continue as Beijing claims almost all of the South China Sea, a conduit for more than $3 trillion of annual shipborne commerce, including parts claimed by the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Brunei.
Parts of the South China Sea that fall within Philippine territory have been renamed by the government as West Philippine Sea to reinforce the country’s claim.

The West Philippine Sea refers to the maritime areas on the western side of the Philippine archipelago including Luzon Sea and the waters around, within and adjacent to the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.
In 2016, the Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague ruled in favor of the Philippines over China's claims in the South China Sea, saying that it had "no legal basis."
China has refused to recognize the decision. —KG, GMA News
